activityComparison.activity: 10.1 Using a Compass to Estimate Length
activityComparison.original: Draw a measured 40° angle, use compass to make both ray sides 5 cm, connect the free endpoints and decide whether third side is longer or shorter than 5.
activityComparison.repair: Replaced unrelated 3/7/11 opening with directly relevant 40° 5 cm included-angle construction and original SVG. Independent math oracle gives BC≈3.42 cm, though Grade 7 students need only compass comparison.

activityComparison.activity: 10.2 Revisiting How Many Can You Draw?
activityComparison.original: Explore 40° angle with two sides 4 and 5 cm and two 6 cm sides with 100° angle using manipulatives and justify uniqueness/multiplicity.
activityComparison.repair: Rich V2 explicitly requires attachment of sides and angle, including one unique included 100°-6/6 example and a separate mathematically exact 45°-8/6 nonincluded two-solution analogue. Original applet's precise student traces not verified; this is not full task parity.

activityComparison.original: Construct 50°/60°/70° triangles with different scales and attempt 50°/60°/100° triple.
activityComparison.repair: Existing generic length examples replaced with original drawing task and SVG two distinct-size triangles with same 50°/60°/70° and explanation of impossible 50°/60°/100°.

activityComparison.original: Use point, segment and compass tools to make a triangle that remains equilateral when vertices are dragged.
activityComparison.repair: Not delivered; required authentic dragging and constraints remain shared-integration / source-parity blocker.

studentTask: Construct original 40° angle with two 5-cm ray segments and compass-check its third side. Draw two 6-cm sides with a 100° included angle and overlay a peer's matching construction. Construct the 45°-8-cm-6-cm nonincluded-angle example using a 6-cm compass circle, mark and measure BOTH valid intersections, then compare the resulting triangles. Draw two different-sized 50°/60°/70° triangles, reject 50°/60°/100° using measured ray closure, and submit diagrams and justifications for teacher evaluation.

criteria.description: Accurate original 40-degree angle with two 5 cm sides, compass estimate and teacher-checkable measurements.
Construct both intersections for the 45°, AB8, BC6 conditions, measure distinct third sides and justify that both fulfill the same attached input constraints.
Draw two distinct scales of valid 50/60/70 triangle and show 50/60/100 is impossible; use an appropriate geometry explanation without requiring formal theorem memorization.
Use units, correct attachment of rays, construction trace, self-check and written/oral reasoning; explain included versus nonincluded angle geometry.
